title: Every EHR, by the specialty it was built for
summary: 95 EHR and practice management systems in 13 specialties, from hospital systems to dental, home health and API-first platforms. Pick your specialty and see which systems you will meet, and which have a prior auth workflow built in.
body_markdown:
When a practice asks us to automate their prior auths, the first question is which EHR they run. The answer depends almost entirely on specialty. So we drew[the map by specialty](https://asteroid.ai/market-maps/ehr) .


## Pick your specialty


The page opens with a sentence: “I run a ___ practice. Which systems will I meet?” Pick behavioral health and you get fifteen systems. Pick dental and you get ten, none of which the ambulatory world has heard of. Pick oncology and you get six, two of them radiation planning systems that double as the chart.


Thirteen specialties in all: acute care, ambulatory, behavioral health, oncology, dental, home health and hospice, long-term care, pediatrics, specialty ambulatory, rehab and therapy, surgical, emergency and EMS, and API-first platforms.


## Where prior auth lives


Hover a logo and the card tells you how that system handles prior auth. Thirteen have a PA workflow built in: Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth and the big ambulatory platforms, plus a few surprises in specialty. Nine route it through an embedded partner, usually CoverMyMeds, Surescripts or DrFirst for drugs and Availity for medical.


In the other 73 we found nothing. Prior auth happens outside the chart, in a portal, a fax queue or a spreadsheet. The practices that run those 73 systems are where a browser agent earns its keep.


## Age of the installed base


The founding-year chart at the bottom shows 61 of these vendors were founded before 2010. The 19 founded since 2015 are mostly API-first, virtual-care and behavioral products, not hospital systems. The chart that runs a hospital was designed before the iPhone.
